intermediate_failure_causes: Two fixtures encoded wrong expectations: the tiny-holdout case could still satisfy the minimum it declared, and the universe-size case assumed the full identifier cross product although the universe is deliberately restricted to identifiers present in the known graph. Both expectations were corrected; the module behaviour was unchanged.
fail_closed_cases: primary feature absent for every candidate
estimator: fixed-budget precision/recall/average precision with a degree-prior baseline from the scored partition
test_substitutes: synthetic 20x15 identifier grid with a planted latent binding rule
scope_limit: Novel binding/PPI work is now delivered as what it can honestly be: unvalidated candidate generation with a held-out evaluation that refuses to be meaningless. Known edges of a declared evidence arm are split by a seeded hash of the edge identity alone, the candidate universe excludes every scored known edge while keeping the held-out ones unmarked, and the additive score uses declared weights and frozen standardisation so nothing is fitted on the evaluation labels. Evaluation reports fixed-budget precision, recall, average precision and the same numbers for a degree-prior baseline built only from the scored partition. Label-like feature columns, duplicate feature rows, an all-missing primary feature, an empty holdout, a partition overlap and a budget larger than the universe are refused. Every emitted row is labelled unvalidated_candidate with orthogonal experimental validation required, and the record states that a ranked candidate is not evidence of binding. The synthetic fixture plants a latent binding rule to check that the estimator has power; it is not real binding data. No acquisition, optimizer, real cohort, paid compute or deployment ran, and no existing binding/PPI graph was modified.
